issue.title: iOS 26 simulator slices missing from libmdk_uniffi.a
issue.body:
Building for any iOS 26 simulator target (Xcode 16+, iOS 26.x runtime) fails because `libmdk_uniffi.a` does not include `arm64-apple-ios-simulator` slices built against the iOS 26 SDK.

**Error:**
```
ld: building for iOS Simulator-arm64 but attempting to link with file built for iOS-arm64
```

**Environment:**
- Xcode 16.x (iOS 26.2 / 26.4 runtime)
- Apple Silicon Mac
- mdk-swift `main` branch (MDK 0.8.0)

**Workaround:**
Build targets a physical device instead of the simulator. Device builds work correctly.

**Request:**
Re-compile `libmdk_uniffi.a` with iOS 26 simulator slices included and push an updated `main` (or tag a release).

Happy to test a build if you need a guinea pig.

comment.body:
Thanks @sjmcnamara, that confirms it.

Your numbers line up exactly with what I pulled from LFS on my end: 570 `IOSSIMULATOR` objects with blank `sdk` (those are the Rust `.rcgu.o` files), 44 with `sdk=26.2`, and the same 5 stragglers at `sdk=18.5` (sqlite3, secp256k1, precomputed_ecmult, precomputed_ecmult_gen, lax_der_parsing, all `cc`-driven C deps).

Every single object is `platform=IOSSIMULATOR` and not one carries the `IOS` device tag, so Xcode 26's "iOS Simulator-arm64 but ... iOS-arm64" message is misleading: the actual rejection is the `sdk=18.5` / `sdk=26.2` mix inside a single archive, and `ld` falls back to that generic platform-mismatch string when it gives up. Xcode 26.4.1 being current stable means anyone on the latest toolchain hits this.

Fix is at marmot-protocol/mdk#312: pin the Swift packaging job to `macos-26-arm64` (default Xcode 26.2), so every C dep compiles against the iOS 26 SDK and the archive stays internally consistent.

`IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0` and `platforms: [.iOS(.v15)]` aren't moving, so iOS 15+ device builds are unaffected.

comment.body:
I dug into the published xcframework on mdk-swift@main and the simulator slice is actually there and structurally tagged correctly: pulled the .a via LFS, extracted all 619 object files, and every single one carries LC_BUILD_VERSION platform=iossimulator. 

So the slice isn't missing, but I do see one thing that's likely tripping up Xcode 26's stricter linker: the sim archive mixes objects built against iPhoneSimulator 18.5 SDK (sqlite/secp256k1 C deps) with objects built against iPhoneSimulator 26.2 SDK (other C deps). That's because our GitHub Actions runner is macos-latest (= macos-15-arm64, default Xcode 16.4), and only some of the cc-driven C deps reach for a newer xcrun.

I have a patch landing that moves the Swift packaging job to macos-26-arm64 so the whole archive ends up consistently sdk=26.x. That should resolve what you're hitting. Once it merges, the master push will republish mdk-swift@main automatically.

In case the fix doesn't work, can you confirm two things so I'm sure I'm chasing the right cause and not just a coincident symptom?

1. Full linker error; the snippet you pasted is cut off; could you re-run with verbose linking and paste the complete ld: line(s)? Specifically I want to see the file path it names, e.g. ... file `/.../libmdk_uniffi.a(sqlite3.o)` for architecture arm64. That'll tell me whether ld is rejecting our archive or a different transitive dependency.

2. `lipo -info` on both slices, from inside your DerivedData / Package cache, and, while you're there, your exact Xcode version:

```bash
cd ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/<YourProj>-*/SourcePackages/checkouts/mdk-swift/Binary/mdk_uniffi.xcframework
lipo -info ios-arm64/libmdk_uniffi.a
lipo -info ios-arm64-simulator/libmdk_uniffi.a
xcodebuild -version
```
